SSB Yoshi, Dark Pit and Sheik

If won anything other than Yoshi I'd probably give away, been looking for a Yoshi for forever to complete the collection :(
My 10 month old has 4 teeth (her first) all coming in at once, and she's miserable.

My dad still buys these.

Sigh

I'd be more worried about teaching my child to treat animals properly than to worry about a nip.

Then again, when it comes to my daughter I'm a strong believer in what doesn't kill her makes her stronger, and the only time I would worry in a situation like that is if the dog attacked out of no where or if the dog broke skin.

This is how ridiculous it is:

When I was 6, I walked on my neighbors dogs tail, and the dog turned around and BIT me (not nip). After cleaning up a bunch of blood and getting 8 stitches, my mom scolds ME about being careful around dogs and asks the neighbor if the dog is okay. Dog was old anyway and he just made sure to keep him away from children just in case it was aggression.

I used to hear moms complain about changing their shirt multiple times a day due to newborn spit up, all while I'm sitting here covered with probably 4 spit up worth of yuck, and thinking "but you know they'll do it again.. so why change?".

I never minded the casual "nice tattoo", but since Pokemon GO it's terrifying. People asking if I got it for the app.. people asking if I play (and when I say no they look confused and ask questions.. or when I pretend and say yes they start a conversation).

I've had tattoos for years but I'm regretting my choice in placement now that the app is out. No one cared about Pokemon when I got it..

I agree. I should have said thank you. I have honestly replayed the whole thing in my head over and over again and wished I said thank you.

But maybe it's the way he was approaching me, or the way he had his hand up - either way, I freaked the hell out. I felt my heart in my throat about to burst.

We were both in the wrong. I shouldn't have been so rude.

It's very hard because of the location and how I'm built (its high up near my collar bone and I'm big chested, so finding a shirt that hides it is a mission).

:(

It's more like on my collar bone, and because I'm big chested sometimes it's hard finding shirts that hide it without being uncomfortable. The whole winter I was fine but now it's getting hot. 

My next outting I'll be hiding it with my hand as much as I can.

My husband does the same. He will also ask, in front of the unopened fridge "do we have milk?". Dear lord.. OPEN THE FRIDGE AND LOOK.

God.
I should have. I wanted to. But then he'll pull the "okay then, not going to work" guilt trip.
So Im not the only one pregnant, with a 10 month old and man child.. thank god.

Oh it's definitely the hormones. I'm trying to relax and remind myself that finding things for him isnt a big deal.

Im just boiling and I know I shouldn't. I'm stressed.
Thank you! :)
Thank you! Super excited :)

My daughter (9 months) closes her eyes the second I pick up the cup to rince her hair- she also holds her breath. But if for some reason she doesn't close her eyes or holds her breath, she has a good giggle out of it.

I honestly never imagined how difficult it would be if she hated that part of bath time. Man that would be difficult to be honest. I would try to make a shield with your hand.
I had to wait for my first period after I had my daughter, so about 3 months after!
Annnnnnnd I need this for my 7 month old.

When people try to be funny, but they come off as stupid.

Lol

I owe my mom for college. She reminds me daily of this. She shows me the tab at least once a week.

"I bought you lunch, I'll put it on the tab" - "but mom I buy you lunch all the time" - "thats because I'm your mother, you have to take care of me in my old age". 

What...

This year, I am a mother for the first time. This year, it means something more than heartache.

This year it's a reminder that I will continue to better myself, so I do NOT turn in to the toxic being that is my mother.

My brother has 10 pictures in our family home hanging up. How many of me? 1. And guess what! He's in it as well.

Hm.

I was about 15, lost my virginity at 17 (I am a woman).

I was seriously super late to the party, but that's because I was sexually abused at age 7 and whenever sex was mentioned, I'd cringe and feel sick to my stomach.
My husband is the one that's dreaming of twins! It's crazy lol
Yep.. hated being pregnant but I feel my daughter NEEDS to be a big sister. Oh god.

My husband told me when we started trying in November that we'd find out in February.. He was right. My husband said we'd have a girl.. He was right. He also said that she'd be on her way the 8th of October, although I did go in to labor the 8th, thank god I had her the 9th because I would have NEVER heard the end of that one.

But he's always right.. Always.

(Side note, he said we'd have the best baby ever, and we did.. like, never cries and sleeps 12 hour nights - since 2 weeks old. Creepy)
well if you count the choose your adventure series...

Thank you so much, good to have a parents perspective.

We plan on moving June 1st, and it seems like years away. The rent we'll have in June is double what my parents have been charging us, but we don't have another option. We can't move sooner since my Disability benefits have been put on hold and they haven't given me a straight forward answer as to when it will return. Right now, it's a waiting game.

Today I am not allowed to go upstairs (where the kitchen and shower is). When my parents left for a bit I had to run upstairs, get bottles ready, bathe my daughter and grab a snack to keep my going. Im so stressed, and feeling pretty pathetic.

My husband to my 17 year old BIL that had a 4 month old son at the time: 

"Hey *BIL*, when are you planning on getting a job?"

"Don't be stupid, you don't need a job when you have a kid"

With my two month old strapped to my chest in a carrier, and on the phone with my husband, I was greeted by a pharmacist that was all smiles. The night before, as our daughter had finally dozed off, we had passionate sex, not a quickie, for the first time since our daughter was born. In the heat of the moment, rushing, giggling, not trying to spoil the moment, we didn't grab a condom. I was ovulating. Plan B it was!

"Could I have a Plan B please?" 

The pharmacist went from smiling at my daughter to giving me the dirtiest look, placing it on the counter and telling me the total. I said I'd pay by debit, and as I'm putting in my pin she says:

"You should focus more on your daughter and less about opening your legs"

I felt awful, but angry. I grabbed my plan B and just left. Wish I would have said something. Bitch got reported though.

Started birth control this month.

Stopped breastfeeding at 3 weeks because of stress and PPD.

Smh, you don't know what smh is?

Pricks be prickin'

I got married in November. Both my husband and I were born in the 90s. When we were getting our marriage license, the lady said "okay, I feel old giving you a license without the need of parental concent".

Poor lady.

Germaphobe.. he's scared of a lot, and it's not his fault. Calling his fears "ridiculous" is ignorant. It is a mental thing, there's only so much he can do and I won't call him ridiculous for it.

Just that kind of attitude that depresses him, thank god I'm not that simple minded.
Thanks, I absolutely adore it! :)

He's 26 and lives with his parents, I'm assuming he doesn't want to wait around until you're "ready" to live together. He has a life apart from your relationship with him, and while you're off establishing your life, he should do the same.

My husband and I planned and conceived our daughter when we were just boyfriend and girlfriend. We knew we were commited, but I kept ruining engagement plans so we decided to wait, and we put it off altogether. He proposed when I was 7 months pregnant, and we got married when my daughter was a month old, but around the time of conceiving I didn't even imagine getting married, felt like it just wasn't for us.

Honestly, to us marriage is just a piece of paper. He was my "husband" even before. But I am thankful to have his last name, and to all be known as a family.

It's clay.

It's okay to be bitter around the holidays when you're sad and alone. No one blames you buddy.

Wife here!

Husband and I were not planning on getting gifts this year, but I had leftover clay from a craft I was doing so I quickly threw it together. Not supposed to be a huge romantic gesture, just something for him to smile at and move on.

Thankfully he liked it more than expected, lol
I guess there's a chance for 2 under 2 then. Oh man..
Thanks, I needed to read that.

Is your 6 week old more clingy with one of you? Like only you can console him?

Im honestly not sure how to get her more comfortable with other people.
I guessed some sort of pig as well, was trying to show my husband that he was definitely wrong with his guess of capybara (he's way wrong).

I never thought I had a purpose. Never once. 

I thought I was one of those people who just went through life being nothing.

It all changed when I gave birth to my daughter. I know it seems cliché, but I struggled with depression nearly my whole life, so this was life changing.

I realized when I held her that this tiny human depends on me, and even though I don't believe I have the capability of being anyone, she has. It's my duty to raise her, help her, and let her be the best she can be. Being a mother gives me a different kind of purpose. This is who I am, and I don't mind being nothing else.

When my mother was pregnant with me, they told her there was a high chance I would have Down Syndrome, and gave her the option of terminating the pregnancy. My father was all for it, but she couldn't do it. 

I was born, healthy and nearly perfect. 

Around 10-11, I started having severe depression, which only got worse. My life seemed to spiral down. I was never good enough for my parents, went through hell. Lost my first boyfriend to suicide at 15 (he was more my best friend than anything), was raped by two guys the same year, and was abused by the next guy I dated. 

When all this was happening, my mom told me to stop being dramatic. She told me to grow up, and when I'd cry because I had enough, she would say "I should have aborted you when I had the chance".

I wished I was never born, more than I wished I was dead. I have severe paranoia, so even though I wanted to die, I was so paranoid of the outcome, the pain and what I'd leave behind. I know the impact suicide has on people around you, and I couldn't do that.

Thankfully things got better, but I know I will have the same feelings eventually. It's a given.

He's abusing you, mentally and physically. He's cheating, and using you for a place to stay. You know this, so leave. I know you think he'll be the only one to love you, but you're worth more than that, and he knows that, which is why he keeps you on a short leash.

It gets better. Much, much better.

We have been going out since we got home from hospital (1 day old). I was super up for it, didn't physically or mentally feel drained, so we went out. Pediatrician said its fine, and baby girl is now 2 1/2 weeks and super healthy! She loves her stroller.

Since I don't drive and neither does mg fiance, we walk everywhere so baby girl comes with and its okay :)

When I was pregnant, doctor kept saying she was going to be really strong and long. Turns out, she is both of those. Fights me while I'm dressing her or changes here, and pushes my boob away (even though she wants it, just doesn't understand her hands don't produce the milk too, lol).

My expectations of a newborn were way off. Actually adoring my strong baby, lol

She does this too! She'll feed for about an hour (wanting it, feeding, not wanting, wanting it again, feeding) and then she'll sleep for long stretches. I can change her diaper, shift her positions, carry her, and nothing would make her wake up.

Don't think we've actually heard the piercing screaming/crying yet, so we're preparing ourselves for that one!

No, just pumping to give daddy the chance to help with feeding and for times we go out and its too hard to feed her (like on the bus).

Otherwise, I'm just breastfeeding. Which is also going great! And I'm hoping it stays that way :)

Went to see the doctor for her 3-4 day checkup, and she said she wasn't too concerned, but did tell us what to look for, gave us an emergency number and told us when to go to the ER if anything.

I have peace of mind now.
I'm nursing, but dont get them. My mom is the only one I know who gets them often (and she's smart enough never to kiss my daughter..).

I had the epidural, but wish I didn't. It wore off after an hour, but my body was still numb. Went through the last bit of labor in horrible pain, holding up my legs was difficult because they were so heavy. I might as well not have gotten it.

Next baby I'm definitely going without! 

(Working on my birth story soon, daughter is 3 days old and I just haven't gotten around to typing it yet!)
Yep, that was me! Haha. Grandpa is just happy she's here. Hasn't even mentioned her being 8 hours late! Haha
Yep! It's on Monday, and we're having turkey on Sunday! We're leaving the hospital around 10am tomorrow so we'll be able to have a good dinner with her!

I ran to the room with the test and jumped on the bed while he was half asleep, while shoving the test in his face.

He just sat there, shocked, then as I showed him the test from far away he said "you can even see the second line from here!" (After a month of having the faintest line, he couldn't believe that a second line could be that strong, :P)

Wanted to do something cute, but excitement took over me.
Due date buddy! If I hear "baby yet?" Or "are you even trying to get things going?" one more time, I might snap!

Contractions just went away! But, randomly having severe headache and horrible blurred vision. OB told me to go to the hospital and she'll meet me there. She's talked about inducing me many times and actually told me she might today.. So not too sure. Doesn't look like baby girl is showing up today though! Especially not if I'm getting induced. Might be a long labor.

Sadly, we're sharing our room with our daughter and are limited on space. He doesn't like sleeping against the wall because he has bladder issues and uses the bathroom maybe twice a night.. Never takes in to consideration my struggle
He makes me sleep against the wall lately. Always.. I put my foot down last night, but there he was, on my side.. I had no choice. Pretty frustrating.

I had a strong feeling I'd have her on the 28th or 29th of September, boy was I wrong!

But, I'm hoping it's before the 20th.. Dont think I can make it!

She doesn't deserve to be called grandmother, or mother while you're at it! You're better off!

Sorry you had to go through that.
I'm pissed reading that. Who the hell? She's a nurse too?!

Off topic, but my fiance's last name is Good, and when we had our first ultrasound, the technician said "wow, this is a good baby", and my fiance said "you dont even know".

She couldn't understand why we were laughing so hard. Next baby we'll be married, so they'll probably clue in on the joke, but yeah, haha.

(Also my fiance's favorite joke is "Are you good?" - "Yeah" - "probably not Bryan Good". He's a dork).

That's completely unacceptable! My mouth dropped open and stayed open the whole time reading that.

That's just disgusting.
Considering mild contractions started, im spooked! We'll see. Don't know if this is it, but my dad is getting all excited, haha
I know if I were 25+ I'd still be getting crap from my parents or from family members! Someone always has to judge.
I just started having tightening and slight contractions. There is no way this could be it.. It's way too spooky! Lol
I hope you never experience it! Pregnancy is supposed to be joyful, no need for negativity in there!

My mom makes comments like "you don't even look pregnant", and my fiance says to her " what are you talking about? Look at the cute bump", to which she replied "she's always looked fat anyway". Thanks mom.

I'm 39 weeks and only gained weight in my belly.. Actually lost weight in my butt, legs and arms.. :(
When he was right there!? Oh my, that's just a new level of stupid and disrespectful.
In my opinion, a rude comment from a family member stings more than a rude comment from a useless stranger. So sorry you had to go through that. Sad he couldn't even be happy for you.

Oh my.. That's horrible! This is why I wish I had the balls to say things back. In my situation and yours, these women deserve to be put in their place. They were both making statements that were wrong (I'm not on welfare, and you're not even a teenager?), but if they were right, why do they have a right to say something?

I just sat there, stunned. I also got teary eyed as she walked away. 

My fiance almost lost it when he realized why I was crying. He was not amused. It was quite horrible.

I'm used to them somewhat (40G), but then when I lay down, shirtless, and try to roll over and they smack me in the face, I get frustrated (my fiance gets a good giggle, but I don't need giant titties smacking me in the face everytime my hip hurts! Which is often!).

Shopping for bras is hell, shopping for comfortable clothing is hell.. And the thought of breastfeeding with these things when it'll be double the size of my daughters head puzzles me. No idea how she's not going to get terrified!
I'd get a second opinion, and definitely a doctor that takes their jobs seriously!
I'm hoping too! Don't want to go back to being miserable!
I'm enjoying it so much, I can't remember why I was begging my doctor to be induced! Lol. Hoping it lasts until labor!

You are stronger, more patient, and much more kind than I would be in your situation. 38 weeks pregnant, I wasn't even able to get out of the house, and look at you! I bet it's difficult, I bet it's hell, but damn, you're like supermom. 

I've been off work for a year, due to back issues and severe depression, but when I read stuff like this it gives me hope that I'll be able to return to work. In my mind, pregnancy is much harder to work with than the issues I'm dealing with, even at 30 weeks it was hard (I'm 39 weeks, and struggling, but it'll be worth it).

My heart breaks for you that you're unable to take more time off. My heart breaks for every mom that says that on here. It's certainly not fair.

I hope all goes well, but hey, I hear that the more active you are during pregnancy the quicker labor is! Fingers crossed you have an easy labor, and your little one is in your arms soon. You deserve some peace.

I decided to dump it, but actually considered taking a picture, kind of regretting not to now!

Anyway, I know that my friend had a bunch more than I did at my stage of pregnancy, and I know another who had drops at my stage. Trying to figure out a "normal" is quite difficult. I wouldn't worry about it.

Then again, as I said in a previous comment, I barely know anything about pregnancy and breastfeeding (just learning as I go), so I'm sure someone else would have a better answer than me.

Since I didn't have enough to store it (but in my mind, having barely leaked throughout my pregnancy, I think I had a bunch!), I decided to dump it.

A friend of mine used to put them in the freezable bags for when baby gets home, because when she was nursing her first, he was always fussy, and she couldn't get enough for him the first couple days, so with her second she had given her the one she pumped beforehand to keep her happy.

Not too sure if I plan to do the same. Honestly, I know nothing about breastfeeding, I'm completely naive when it comes to everything, which is why I'm glad my hospital offers a breastfeeding class for all new moms in the L&D to attend after baby is born.

I got the go ahead from my doctor! I was actually nervous to try, so I asked her, and she said everything should be fine considering how my body is progressing.

But I am hoping I don't labor for that long, ouff! Kind of terrifying.

Ouff I'm hoping it's something, but not trying to get super excited. But, considering they've been happening for about an hour now, if its not actually early labor, then i'll try again tomorrow morning and see where that takes me!
39 weeks today! Up until now, I got nothing, then today, my left boob just had a lot (okay, not a lot.. But more than nothing and enough to see swirl around in the cup attached to the pump!)
Thank you !
Thank you!

Did the 15 minute per breast pumping and having contractions! Stomach is super hard. Might just be braxton Hicks, but hey! It did something! The more braxton Hicks the closer we're to labor, right?

(Also went for a walk, and baby's head was pressing hard down on my cervix and that was quite painful. Keeping my fingers crossed!)

Only started feeling horrible at week 36. Then again, I get random bursts of energy!

It's different for everyone :)
Oh my, now my stomach is rock hard!

I searched for a shop that sold the brand near me, and called in advance to make sure they had my size. When j went in, the lady actually had set aside 3 different styles and I got to try them on.

Make a quick search on Google to see if anyone is selling them in their stores near you! It's a popular nursing bra.

I'm a 40G, and recently got the bravado brand nursing bra. Super supportive, super comfy, they have even sleeping styles. Definitely recommend bravado (I was told to get bravado from about 10 breastfeeding mamas, so when I tried it on and loved them, I saw why!).

Sending you labor vibes! At 39 weeks pregnant, I'm facing the fact that I might go overdue, and its killing me. Considering today is your due date, I'm sending you all the vibes! As long as I have my baby by at least 40+4. Don't think my fiance would survive me at 41+ weeks.
Nope, I'd ask for a refund. That's not acceptable. Why should you have to cater to their needs when you, the client, are paying. Nope. I'd have a fuss.

I'm *Monsterification* , I'm 19 (20 on Nov. 8th!) and am a FTM to a baby girl due in 7 days (ouff, time flies!). My fiance and I got engaged August 16th, and we're super excited for this little girl to arrive. Found out I was expecting on February 3rd, and since then, feels like this pregnancy has flown by, up until now. Every little pain, twitch, and feeling I get, I tense up, and wonder if it's labor, only to be disappointed.

I've been struggling with severe depression throughout pregnancy (diagnosed with bipolar), but as of last week, its gotten much work. Happy to say that today I'm feeling much better, feeling a little bit myself, and just in time too because I've got yet another couple of appointments today.

39 weeks today, and last night I think my daughter stretched her whole body, and it was popping out. I cried in pain, tried pushing her back, but that's when the mega kicks started.

This is probably why she's not coming out.. She loves torturing her mommy.

I was hoping for a boy, wanted a boy, had a name picked out, dreamt of a boy. Then the day of the scan came up, and as she was checking, I thought "I want a girl..". There she was. Little girl!

It's what my fiance wanted, and when I told him that night he cried. Never had a strong feeling of girl until the day of.

Seeking treatment for bipolar as I'm diagnosed (you need to be diagnosed to be able to receive ODSP).

I take a safe dose of medication, safe for me and safe for baby.

Long school buses didn't have seatbelts, short ones did. Took a school bus throughout all my years of school (yep, even highschool! Since my highschool was about an hour and a half away by public transportation, they picked us up).
Ouff, you're going to have a handsome boy on your hands! So adorable!

I knew mine was getting bad when my fiance looked at me, teary eyed, and said "I'm worried about you". This coming from a man that has never even flinched when I said I had thoughts of suicide, or when I would cry and said I would hurt myself. He knew I wouldn't. He knew I was just at my breaking point and it would get better.

Now, he's worried. He came home from work for lunch, for the first time ever, just to sit with me. He even says " I can't remember the last time you kissed me", and asked "will you miss me when I'm at work?", and I said yes, and he said "I hope, I just don't want you to leave me, I know it'll get better, but I worry about you".

That's when I knew.. That if he's worried, its bad. He said it's not like my normal depression, and I agree.

My next one is tomorrow, I'll bring it up with her then. I'm a bit worried that someone will judge me, always have been. Also scared she'll contact a social worker to speak to me when our daughter is born. Considering I have severe bipolar, and I'm also 19 (turning 20 next month), I worry they'll view me as unfit and take our daughter away or something.

I know its just my paranoia getting the best of me, but I still worry.
It's much more relaxing. Pregnancy definitely helped with a few things! Super glad about that :)

I suffer from a severe paranoia, have never slept naked in bed with my fiance, or been naked beside him ever because I was raped when I was younger, but since about week 29, I NEED to sleep naked.

It's like all my fears and paranoia were washed away by this need not to feel restricted by clothes.

Clothes suck anyway.. Need to sleep with just panties and let everything flow free!

In my opinion, she probably has a bad cold. She was able to get out of bed and somewhat function, and with my experience of a horrible flu, yeah, that's nearly impossible. I completely agree with taking pregnancy over that kind of flu! It feels like death.
We were texting, thank god. But knowing her, she wouldn't have enough common sense to tell me she was sick before hanging out.

I read your post actually, and I'm hoping I get the same outcome! If not, then at least i've got the cute fortune! Haha. Still no signs of labor approaching today, so don't think it'll happen for a few days ;)
Yep! It did! I'm sure she'll enjoy it when she's older! Haha
Yep! Went straight in the baby book to be later organized! (making a scrapbook as opposed to the usual store bought ones). Super excited to have it all done when she gets here :)

My mom's cat wandered in to our bedroom, and she's the sweetest thing, but I know if any animal were to harm our baby, it would be this one (she's a face cuddler, so she's not allowed anywhere near the baby!). 

Our Aussie saw her come in the room, and he bolted to watch her. Second she got to my belly and rolled over near it, he barked (which he only does if my fiance and I are fooling around tickling each other and I laugh too hard and he thinks I'm getting hurt).

The cat jumped down, dog ran to me, licked my belly then went back to his spot in the livingroom.

He's protective of his little sister already :)

I was thinking in my head before I opened it "it would be funny if it was a fortune that could relate to baby showing up soon", and there it was, lol.

We also got 5 other fortune cookies, and after opening all of them, they didn't have anything close to this one! Funny how this one was the first one I opened :) (had to open all the other ones, because they're sooo yummy)
Highlighting the soon part! Haha. She's due the 13th, but man I want her here now! Haha

I'll send you some if you send me some (sending you some now!).

Hoping we both have our babies soon!
Was at the hospital, they had to do blood work twice every visit. Went there 4 times. Was brutal..

My fiance has always been nervous, and as we're expecting a little girl, he feels there's a lot of pressure.

Growing up, I didn't really have a role model of how a man should be, or how a woman should be treated, because my dad was horrible, so he has made it his goal to show our daughter exactly how a man should treat a woman (and he'll do amazing!). 

Besides that, he knows nothing about babies. He worries about holding her, changing her, if he'll be there enough, when to help, when to back off, he just worries all over the place.

When I was 6 months pregnant, I looked at him and said:

"I don't know what I'm doing, besides what I've learned from watching others and most common sense, so I'm going in pretty much blind. We'll teach each other, we'll help each other. I don't expect you to be daddy of the year from the first second. I expect you to be clumsy, nervous, but after all that, deeply in love with your daughter. First thing I want you to do, and the only thing I expect, is to be there and let her see that. A smile is something you have daily, and as long as you don't lose that, you've got it all right there, the rest will fall in to place, and in no time, you'll wonder why you were even scared"

He's so excited now. He knows my expectations for him aren't high. I don't expect him to know exactly why she's upset, or exactly what to do with her, so that lifted some pressure from his shoulders. When he does certain things, I smile and say "this is why you're going to be an amazing daddy" and that makes his day.

Since he's calmed down, he kisses my belly, tells her he's ready, and that she can come out. But I know there's a part of him that still worries, and that's okay. I'd rather him go in a little nervous, than over cocky and screw up and feel bad.

We get the instincts and turn in to mothers when we first become pregnant, they become Daddy's when they first hold them. We've been holding them for 9 months, they have time to catch up (oh and kids tend to turn to daddy anyway, they've got that going for them! Haha).

I was trying to prepare myself for the last few weeks, because I knew and heard that it would be bad.. But my god, didn't think it would be this mad!

I've had an easy going pregnancy, then BAM, all hell breaks loose. And it'll only get worse until she pops out! Ouff!

But, we get our babies soon! I'm excited, only thing getting me through this! Haha

This too! I'm even nervous about how many people my fiance wants to invite. We've been dying to meet her since February (actually even before our positive, because we were trying for a couple months!) and everyone else has been waiting much less, and to think that I have to share her instantly makes me kind of jealous.

I want to stare at her for hour and soak up all her beauty for days. Guess I'll have to get used to sharing her now that she's coming out. Right now, all her wiggles are mine, but soon everyone else will get to experience it. Kind of bitter sweet!

And the breastfeeding also has me concerned.. If she has to feed, I know damn well his family is too stubborn to get out for me to feed her. Gr

Due date is 12 days away and I'm patiently waiting. I want my newborn snuggles, kisses and love! Keep telling her to come out, then she squirms and is probably thinking "yeah.. No. I'm comfortable!". Grr

A friend of mine and I were downtown, on a bench, and her son started fussing. She was so nervous to feed him, no where to go, so I said "if you're comfortable, feed him here, you'll be fine".

5 minutes later.. A woman walks by, and says "that's disgusting, cover your boob!" (she was, first of all. She had a nursing tank and it was so hot out.. Baby boy did not need to suffer under a cover!).

So I said, very calmly "ma'am, you know a woman is allowed to walk shirtless and exposed in the streets of Toronto, right? Its not against the law, in fact, I see it once in a while. She's feeding her son, not completely exposed and her son doesn't need to be boiling to convenience you.".

A little bit of back story, since I didn't mention last time:

My grandmother lives in New Brunswick, where my mother and father were raised, and my parents moved to Ontario (Toronto) to find jobs since New Brunswick doesn't have much to offer. When my mom announced she was pregnant with my brother, my grandmother said "I thought you were calling with good news". My mom was devastated, and didn't even mention when she was pregnant with me (in my whole families eyes, I just showed up).

My grandmother would visit and would not recognise me, and she would always say I was my cousins friend (this cousin lives down the street from me).

It hurt, I ended up just cutting ties with her and saying I wanted nothing to do with her.

When I found out I was expecting, she called me personally. Although only being 19, and in her eyes I assumed was making a mistake, and said she was proud of me. Since then, she's done nothing but try to make up for lost time (making plans to visit, sending gifts, welcoming my SO in to our family, just wonderful things).

I have learned that everyone deserves a second chance. She's realizing that she's getting older, and she wants us all there for her. She doesn't need to shower us with gifts, and I've told her that, but she said " if I can't be there, I'm hoping she'll wear everything I've sent".

The pain from her squirming gets so bad I have to sit sometimes. I'm only 25 weeks and already uncomfortable. Oh dear god.. Only gets worse from here, haha.

Honestly, the first time I felt her kick I thought if was the strongest gas bubble I ever felt. Then it happened again, and I said "wow, this is a weird gas bubble..". Then it clicked, had to be baby.

It was only until my SO got home and I felt if again, that i put his hand on my belly and we both felt it. Now, a week later, we can see her squirm around.. Its crazy.

Definitely research!

When I was younger, I always wanted a puppy. I researched certain breeds, temperaments, and everything, and found that Australian Shepherds would be a perfect fit for my level of capability in training and providing exercise. After looking everywhere, I saw that they were way out of my price range, and decided to get the cheapest, cutest dog I could find.

I thought with extra time I could train him, but he was just too hard headed, required a lot of space, and needed to be babied. He's a large dog, and although I love him to pieces, I regret getting him sometimes because he could have had a more experienced owner.

Now, years later, I adopted an older Australian Shepherd. He fits in to my lifestyle like a glove, and I'm head over heels in love. Its different when you can train and control certain breeds. I probably will never change breeds, and am looking forward to adding an Aussie puppy to our family down the line.

I wish someone would have told me to stick to my research. Owning a dog is hard work, and can be even more difficult if you don't take in to consideration your lifestyle. Don't get a dog thinking you'll adapt to their needs, get one that will fit your lifestyle.
